research_question: Among children in low- and middle-income countries, what is the effect of mobile phone reminders sent to parents or caregivers—SMS text messages, live phone calls, and/or automated voice calls—compared with routine immunisation care without reminders on receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/DPT3/pentavalent-3/Penta-3)? Include individually randomised and cluster-randomised controlled trials and pool crude intention-to-treat risks using a random-effects risk ratio.
treatment_label: Mobile phone reminders to parents or caregivers (SMS text messages and/or live or automated voice calls) without incentives or other co-interventions
control_label: Routine immunisation care without mobile phone reminders
outcome_description: Binary receipt/completion of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/DPT3/pentavalent-3/Penta-3): number vaccinated out of all participants randomised or enrolled in each eligible arm at the study's main follow-up assessment for that dose. Prefer overall receipt/completion over timeliness or absence of delay; if doses are reported separately, use only dose 3 or completion of all three doses. Extract crude arm-level event counts and intention-to-treat totals. Convert reported percentages to counts using the randomised arm denominator when necessary. For cluster-randomised trials, retain the crude event data and record clustering information for appropriate variance adjustment.
positive_direction: A positive treatment effect (RR greater than 1) means that more children received DTP3/Penta-3 in the mobile-reminder arm than in routine care, favouring reminders.
search_queries: mobile phone SMS reminder childhood DTP3 vaccination randomized trial
text message phone call reminder pentavalent vaccine controlled trial children
caregiver mobile reminder DPT3 immunisation randomised LMIC
inclusion_criteria: Original individually randomised or cluster-randomised controlled trials conducted in a low- or middle-income country and comparing an eligible mobile phone reminder arm with routine immunisation care without reminders.

Interventions consisting of SMS text reminders, live telephone-call reminders, automated voice-call reminders, or a combination of these, directed to a child's parent or caregiver without monetary incentives or other substantive co-interventions in the selected treatment arm.

Studies reporting quantitative arm-level data on overall receipt or completion of DTP3/DPT3/pentavalent-3/Penta-3 at the main follow-up, sufficient to derive vaccinated events and intention-to-treat totals.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, protocols without results, and theoretical papers; also exclude non-randomised studies and controlled before-after studies.
No comparison between an eligible reminder treatment condition and a no-reminder routine-care control condition.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as arm-level events and totals, percentages with denominators, means plus SDs, t/F statistics, proportions, or odds ratios; for this review, exclude reports from which crude DTP3 receipt risks cannot be recovered and do not substitute adjusted odds ratios, logistic-regression estimates, or cluster-adjusted GEE risk ratios for available raw counts.

Completely unrelated to mobile reminders for childhood DTP3-containing vaccination, or reporting only excluded outcomes such as measles, BCG, OPV, yellow fever, fully immunised/all scheduled vaccines, timeliness or delay, or costs; also exclude reminder arms bundled with monetary incentives, education, or other substantive co-interventions when no reminder-only contrast is available.
moderators_to_extract: Reminder modality (SMS, live call, automated voice call, or combined mobile modalities)
Randomisation unit and design (individual versus cluster randomised)
Country and World Bank income classification at the time of the study
Reminder schedule and intensity (number, timing, and frequency of contacts)
Age or vaccination status at enrolment and age/time point at the main DTP3 follow-up
Risk-of-bias domains and control-group DTP3 receipt rate
effect_size_note: Pool crude intention-to-treat risk ratios using a random-effects model, with RR = (DTP3 recipients/all randomised in the reminder arm) divided by (DTP3 recipients/all randomised in routine care). Extract raw events and totals; when only percentages are given, derive counts from the number randomised in that arm using transparent rounding and sensitivity checks if ambiguous. Prefer all randomised/enrolled denominators over per-protocol or follow-up-only denominators. Use the study's primary/main assessment for overall receipt of dose 3 (for example, by 14 or 18 weeks or by 6 or 12 months), not timely receipt when overall receipt is available. In multi-arm trials, include only a reminder-only arm and the no-reminder routine-care arm; ignore incentive-combination, education-only, and other co-intervention arms. Do not convert odds ratios. For cluster trials, use crude risks but adjust the sampling variance for clustering using a reported ICC/design effect or an externally justified ICC in sensitivity analysis; avoid treating individuals as independently randomised. If multiple eligible reminder-only arms share one control, combine eligible reminder arms when clinically appropriate or split the control denominator/events to avoid double counting. Assess heterogeneity with tau-squared, I-squared, and a prediction interval when feasible; use sensitivity analyses for cluster adjustments, imputed counts, and high risk of bias. Assess small-study effects with funnel-plot methods only when enough studies are available. Follow PRISMA 2020 for searching, deduplication, dual screening, extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, study-flow reporting, and synthesis documentation.
single_outcome_target: receipt of the third dose of a DTP-containing vaccine
